newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No Russia deal yet, talks positive-De Beers.
newsitem.headline: No Russia deal yet, talks positive-De Beers.

text.p: De Beers does not expect to reach a final diamond trade deal with Russia this week but will hold informal working group talks, De Beers' Moscow representative said on Monday, adding that recent talks had been constructive.
De Beers met Russia's monopoly diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) last week, said Raymond Clark, general director of De Beers' Moscow representation.
"Last year we said we would be coming back to review our relations with ARS," Clark said. "This is what we were doing last week and we had a pretty constructive few days."
"We anticipate continuing our discussions at working party level this week, but there will be no formal talks," he added.
De Beers also met with Russian government representatives during the latest talks, Clark said.

On Saturday Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits, who took part in Friday discussions, was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying that a compromise had been found "which represents the interests of both Russia and De Beers".
The agency gave no further details of the compromise.
De Beers' Clark said he could not comment on Livshits' remarks, but added that he was encouraged by talks with the Russian government.
"At the end of the week we met with the government again, and they seemed to make some positive noises about the future," Clark said. "Things seem to be moving in the right direction."

ARS is the partner to De Beers in a stalled gem deal. De Beers stopped purchases of Russian diamonds at the end of last year when it cancelled its interim arrangement after Russia failed to approve or reject a new trade deal.
